title: Branwen: The Insult That Started a War
subtitle: A marriage meant to heal — and a kingdom burned for a face-slapped horse

learningObjectives.text: What insult poisons the Irish marriage?

insult.excerpt: And behold one day, Evnissyen, the quarrelsome man of whom it is spoken above, came by chance into the place, where the horses of Matholwch were, and asked whose horses they might be. “They are the horses of Matholwch king of Ireland, who is married to Branwen, thy sister; his horses are they.” “And is it thus they have done with a maiden such as she, and moreover my sister, bestowing her without my consent? They could have offered no greater insult to me than this,” said he. message.locator: The Second Branch, Branwen sends word to her brother; local text normalized characters 420563-421266
message.excerpt: And Branwen reared a starling in the cover of the kneading trough, and she taught it to speak, and she taught the bird what manner of man her brother was. And she wrote a letter of her woes, and the despite with which she was treated, and she bound the letter to the root of the bird’s wing, and sent it towards Britain. And the bird came to this island, and one day it found Bendigeid Vran at Caer Seiont in Arvon, conferring there, and it alighted upon his shoulder and ruffled its feathers, so that the letter was seen, and they knew that the bird had been reared in a domestic manner. narrativeBlocks.title: The bridge of ships
narrativeBlocks.body: Bran the Blessed, giant king of Britain, wades the sea to Ireland for a marriage treaty: his sister Branwen will wed the Irish king Matholwch. The alliance is meant to bind two peoples.

narrativeBlocks.title: The insult that undoes it
narrativeBlocks.body: Bran's half-brother Efnisien, furious he wasn't consulted, mutilates Matholwch's horses — lips, ears, tails. The Irish king treats it as a calculated insult, and the 'peace' is poisoned from the wedding day.

narrativeBlocks.title: Branwen in the kitchen
narrativeBlocks.body: In Ireland, Matholwch's revenge is quiet cruelty: Branwen is demoted to work in the kitchens, her son kept hostage. A starling she trains carries her plea for rescue back to Britain.

narrativeBlocks.title: The war over the sea
narrativeBlocks.body: Bran wades across with his army for the rescue — and Ireland offers peace through trickery, hiding warriors in the hall. The battle that follows destroys almost everyone on both sides.

narrativeBlocks.title: The cost of a horse's ear
narrativeBlocks.body: From a mutilated horse to a war that annihilates two kingdoms: the tale teaches that small insults, unanswered, compound. Branwen dies of grief homecoming, and the surviving Britons flee with Bran's severed — still-talking — head.

quiz.prompt: What insult poisons the Irish marriage?

choices.text: The bride is given a false crown
The feast lacks meat for the guests
Efnisien mutilates Matholwch's horses — the half-brother offended at not being consulted

quiz.explanation: A petty vandalism compounds into war — the tale's warning about unchecked insults.

choices.text: She trains a starling to carry her plea across the sea to Bran
She writes on a birch scroll

quiz.explanation: The trained bird is the detail the tale is famous for.
